sub_questions.question: Why did my credit balance drop faster this week even though I didn't change how I use the app?

claims.claim: Credits are not charged at a flat rate per response.
claims.guide_evidence: Message credits are not consumed at a flat rate.

claims.claim: Lighter models can cost as little as 1 credit per response.
claims.guide_evidence: lighter models (for example smaller GPT variants) consume as little as 1 credit per response

claims.claim: Mid-tier models cost around 5 credits per response.
Heavier or multimodal models (transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat models) cost around 10 credits per response.
claims.guide_evidence: larger or multimodal models (audio transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat models) around 10 credits per response

claims.claim: A shift in the mix of models called can make credits drain faster.
claims.guide_evidence: A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: The customer's team switched the app over to a flagship chat model this week.
That model switch alone explains the faster credit burn.
Usage logs show which model handled the most requests and can confirm the cause.

customer_safety_issues: States as fact that the customer's team switched to a flagship model, which contradicts the customer's own statement that nothing changed
evaluation.rationale: The answer is right that credits are metered per model, with rates of about 1, 5 and 10 credits per response. However, it says as fact that Ingrid's team switched to a flagship model this week. That cause is made up, it contradicts her statement that nothing changed, and she could act on it by chasing a switch that never happened. It also points her to 'usage logs', which the guide never mentions, when it should have asked what changed or which models she uses.
